areas.name: Storelk Mountain
areas.blurb: Storelk Mountain is a summit on the Continental Divide in the Elk Range, on the Alberta-British Columbia border near Highwood Pass. It is a difficult scramble with an untrailed approach in grizzly country.

routes.name: East Face and Ridge
routes.rock_grade: Class 4 on a steep, loose east face and an exposed ridge nose, with scree-covered slab
routes.best_season: Summer through early autumn, once the face is free of snow; larch season in late September is popular.
routes.overview: Storelk is a serious scramble rather than a walk. The approach has no trail and is a bushwhack through dense berry brush, then the route gains a col and climbs a loose east face and a steep ridge nose to the north-south summit ridge. The difficulty rating also reflects the approach, route-finding and bear country.
routes.beta: Start in forest near Highwood Pass. A flagged ribbon at the start may lead to a false trail, so navigate carefully, cross the stream to its south side and climb steep slopes through dense berry bushes. A natural drainage leads up to the col. From the col, cross a meadow to the south and climb the steep, loose east face, detouring along the base of a short cliff band. Higher, a steep, exposed ridge nose reaches the main north-south ridge, which is followed over scree-covered slab, with several no-slip zones, to the summit. Parties using other lines, including the east ridge, have found the crest bushy and the ground steep and loose.
routes.approach: Highwood Pass on Highway 40 in Kananaskis. The route starts in forest near the pass and quickly becomes a route-finding bushwhack; there is no maintained trail to the peak.
routes.descent_text: Stay on the summit ridge rather than traversing below it across loose rubble and slab, then reverse the east face, taking care at the exposed step past the cliff band. A blazed trail marks the final stretch back to the road.
hazards: Class 4 exposed scrambling on loose rock
Rockfall from the loose east face
Grizzly bears in the approach brush
